articles.summary: 3D Systems Expands European Dental Presence Through Partnership with BioSummer Dental Elizabeth Piet Sat, 10/31/2026 - 13:49 Release Date Monday, Nov 2, 2026 7:40 AM BioSummer Dental adds NextDent® 300 MultiJet 3D printers to its distribution portfolio, supporting broader access to digital denture production across France. ROCK HILL, S.C., November 2, 2026 — 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) today announced an expansion of its long-standing strategic distribution partnership with BioSummer Dental, a France-based distributor of advanced digital dentistry solutions. As part of the collaboration, BioSummer Dental has added the NextDent 300 MultiJet 3D printer to its portfolio and is preparing to deliver the first units to several strategic customers, reinforcing its commitment to bringing innovative dental 3D printing technologies to laboratories throughout Europe. The expansion supports 3D Systems' European growth strategy following the achievement of EU Medical Device Regulation (EU MDR 2017/745) certification in April 2026 for the NextDent Jet Base and Teeth materials, enabling commercialization throughout the European Union. With this critical milestone achieved, the Company is now expanding market access through strategic distribution partnerships and helping more dental laboratories transition to efficient, scalable digital denture production. “Expanding our presence in Europe is a key priority for our dental business, and strong distribution partners like BioSummer Dental are essential to that growth,” said Jeff Graves, President and CEO of 3D Systems. “BioSummer Dental’s decision to add the NextDent 300 to its portfolio demonstrates their confidence in our technology and the opportunity ahead for digital denture production. We are pleased to strengthen this partnership as we work together to bring the benefits of the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution to more laboratories, and ultimately, more patients across Europe.” The NextDent Jetted Denture Solution enables laboratories to produce highly aesthetic, durable monolithic dentures through a streamlined, integrated workflow. By simplifying production and reducing labor-intensive manual processes, the solution helps laboratories improve efficiency, increase productivity, and consistently deliver high-quality, patient-specific dentures. Through its established presence in the dental industry and expertise in digital workflows, BioSummer Dental plays an important role in making these capabilities more accessible to dental professionals. The addition of the NextDent 300 positions BioSummer Dental to support broader adoption as laboratories seek more efficient solutions to meet growing production demands. “We are excited to expand our partnership with 3D Systems and add the NextDent 300 to our distribution portfolio,” said Olivier Bellaton, CEO, BioSummer Dental. “Digital denture production represents a significant opportunity for dental laboratories across Europe. We believe the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution offers an exceptional combination of quality, productivity, and ease of use, and we look forward to helping our customers take advantage of this technology.” Together, 3D Systems and BioSummer Dental aim to accelerate the adoption of digital denture workflows, making advanced manufacturing solutions more accessible to dental professionals across France and the rest of Europe. For more information about the NextDent Jetted Denture Solution, visit www.3dsystems.com/dental-jetted-dentures . About 3D Systems For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; data center infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com . About BioSummer Dental BioSummer Dental is a France-based provider and distributor of digital dental technologies and solutions. With a focus on helping dental professionals adopt innovative manufacturing workflows, the company offers technologies designed to support productivity, precision, and efficiency in modern dental laboratories. For more information, visit www.biosummer.com . articles.summary: Finance Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and Payroll in 2026 Oluwakemi Adesina October 31, 2026 The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (effective January 1, 2026) is the governing fiscal legislation that overhauled personal income tax in Nigeria. It replaced the old Consolidated Relief Allowance (CRA) with direct statutory deductions, including a new Rent Relief Allowance capped at ₦500,000, and introduced six progressive tax bands with a 0% rate on the first ₦800,000 of annual chargeable income. Imagine looking at your monthly payroll spreadsheet and realizing that two employees earning the exact same ₦12 million annual salary are walking away with completely different net take-home pay. In the past, that would have meant someone made a calculation error. Today, it means your payroll system is actually working the way it is supposed to. When the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 took effect, it changed the tax setup Nigerian finance teams had relied on for years. The familiar Consolidated Relief Allowance (CRA); that blanket formula that gave every employee a predictable 20% plus ₦200,000 tax shield; was completely thrown out. In its place is a new reality built on direct, verifiable deductions, an ₦800,000 tax-free floor, and a specific Rent Relief Allowance. For business owners, HR managers, and finance leads across Nigeria, this shift changes everything about how you manage payday. This guide breaks down what changed under the 2026 rules, how PAYE calculations actually work now, and how to keep your monthly filings airtight before the taxman comes calling. What Changed Under Nigeria’s Tax Reforms for 2026? The core objective of the Nigeria tax reforms is to align personal taxation with verifiable individual circumstances rather than applying broad arbitrary allowances. The tax-free income threshold now exempts the first ₦800,000 of annual chargeable income at a 0% tax rate. The old Consolidated Relief Allowance of ₦200,000 plus 20% of gross income is completely abolished and replaced by specific, verifiable statutory reliefs. Chief among these is the new Rent Relief Allowance, which allows employees to claim 20% of their actual annual rent paid, subject to a maximum cap of ₦500,000. Furthermore, the progressive personal income tax bands have been restructured across six brackets ranging from 0% to 25%, and the loss of employment severance exemption cap has been increased up to ₦50,000,000. Personal Income Tax and PAYE Pay As You Earn (PAYE) is not a separate business tax; it is the statutory mechanism where employers deduct personal income tax from employee salaries at source. Under the 2026 framework, PAYE is computed on an employee’s chargeable income; the amount remaining after subtracting all allowable statutory deductions and valid reliefs from gross earnings. The progressive annual tax bands applied to chargeable income run as follows: First ₦800,000: 0% (Tax-free floor) Next ₦2,200,000 (₦800,001 to ₦3,000,000): 15% Next ₦9,000,000 (₦3,000,001 to ₦12,000,000): 18% Next ₦13,000,000 (₦12,000,001 to ₦25,000,000): 21% Next ₦25,000,000 (₦25,000,001 to ₦50,000,000): 23% Above ₦50,000,000: 25% Because these bands are progressive, each rate applies strictly to the slice of income within that specific bracket, rather than applying to the entire gross salary. Tax-Free Income Threshold and Applicable Reliefs The ₦800,000 annual tax-free floor fully protects minimum-wage earners and low-income workers from PAYE deductions. For employees earning above this threshold, lowering chargeable income depends on applying valid, documented statutory deductions: Pension Contributions: Statutory employee contributions (8% of pensionable emoluments: Basic, Housing, Transport) remain fully tax-deductible. National Housing Fund (NHF): 2.5% of basic salary, applicable for private-sector staff on an opt-in basis. Health Insurance (NHIA/NHIS): Direct employee contributions to approved health schemes are deductible. Rent Relief Allowance: Employees can claim 20% of their actual annual rent paid, up to an absolute cap of ₦500,000 per tax year. Life Insurance & Owner-Occupier Mortgage Interest: Documented premiums and mortgage interest paid on a primary residence remain allowable deductions. Crucially, rent relief is not an automatic grant. Employees must declare their rent and provide proof such as a tenancy agreement and valid rent receipt. If an employee fails to submit documentation, payroll administrators must set that relief input to zero. How Does the Nigeria Tax Act Affect Employer Payroll? The operational reality of employer tax obligations in Nigeria under the current law is that static salary formulas are dead. Consider those two managers earning an identical gross salary of ₦12,000,000 annually. Manager A submits a verified tenancy agreement showing ₦2,500,000 annual rent, qualifying for the full ₦500,000 rent relief cap. Manager B lives in a family property and pays zero rent. Because Manager A’s chargeable income is ₦500,000 lower, their annual PAYE liability will be noticeably lower than Manager B’s. This variance means finance teams must treat payroll as a dynamic monthly workflow. First, collect and verify employee relief documents before processing begins. Next, calculate net chargeable income using the 2026 progressive bands. Then, run a pre-payroll audit to reconcile any unexpected tax swings against the previous month’s numbers. Finally, disburse net salaries and remit withheld PAYE to the relevant state tax authorities by the 10th of the following month. Failing to remit withheld PAYE on time or misallocating state tax jurisdictions for remote workers triggers immediate interest charges and administrative penalties. Start by auditing your payroll system logic to verify that it applies the 2026 progressive bands and the ₦800,000 zero-tax floor. Next, purge all old Consolidated Relief Allowance formulas (20% + ₦200,000) from active templates and spreadsheets. Collect relief proof by requesting updated tenancy agreements, rent receipts, pension PFA details, and NHF opt-in forms from your staff. Run sample test runs across different salary brackets to ensure net pay outputs match audited expectations.
